title: E-Filing Rejection Reason Checker | What Refused the Return
content:
Transmission

E-Filing Rejection Reason Checker

A refused transmission is usually one of four identifier mismatches. Four answers name the cause and what clears it.

Four answersNames the causeSays what clears itOne corrected transmission included

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

What the return carries

Answer the four questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Rejection Is Not an Assessment

A refused transmission means the return was never received, so the tax year stays exactly as open as it was before. Nothing is assessed, nothing is charged for the refusal itself, and no record of it reaches the corporation’s account.

That is the reason a rejection is worth clearing rather than leaving. It reads like a setback and it is really an unfiled year with a note attached saying which field to fix. A refused transmission also produces no CRA confirmation at all, and the CRA confirmation due date calculator dates the one an accepted transmission does produce.

The Four Identifier Mismatches

CauseWhere the right value comes fromWhat clears it
The legal name does not match the registerThe register the corporation was incorporated underTransmit the exact legal name, corporation number and suffix included
The fiscal year-end does not match the Agency recordThe incorporation record the Canada Revenue Agency holdsSettle the year-end with the Agency, then transmit
The Business Number is not the corporation’s ownThe corporation’s own Canada Revenue Agency recordConfirm the Business Number against the corporation name
The year has already been filed and assessedThe assessment already on the accountAn assessed year is adjusted rather than refiled

The Business Number versus corporation number checker separates the two identifiers these mismatches confuse, and the mandatory T2 e-filing checker covers which tax years have to be transmitted electronically at all.

One Corrected Transmission Is Inside the Fee

Where a first transmission is refused, we read the rejection, correct the return and transmit it again, and that second transmission is included in $300.00 plus HST per tax year rather than charged separately.

What is not inside the fee is an adjustment to a year that has already been assessed. That is a different filing on a year that is already closed, and we say so before you pay rather than after.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why was my T2 rejected?

Most often one of four identifier mismatches: the legal name does not match the register, the fiscal year-end does not match the record the Canada Revenue Agency holds, the Business Number is not the corporation’s own, or the year has already been filed. The checker names which of the four applies to you.

Does a rejected return count as filed?

No. A refused transmission was never received, so the tax year stays open and unfiled until a transmission is accepted. Nothing is assessed and nothing is charged for the refusal itself.

Do I pay again to transmit a corrected return?

No. One corrected transmission is included in $300.00 plus HST per tax year. An adjustment to a year that has already been assessed is a different filing and is not covered.

title: Expenses Only Year Checker | Costs but No Income
content:
Is It Nil

Expenses Only Year Checker

A year with costs and no revenue is still a nil year. Three answers confirm it and name the schedules it triggers.

Three answersCosts do not end a nil yearNames the GIFI triggerInterest does end it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

What the year held

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Money Going Out Is Not Activity

A corporation that paid a bank charge, an annual registry fee or an accounting bill, and took nothing in, had no activity in the sense the nil test uses. The return reports expenses against no revenue, which is a loss for the year rather than income, and it is still a nil return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

The asymmetry is the part worth stating plainly: what ends a nil year is something coming in, not something going out.

What Each Entry Does to the Year

What the year heldStill nil?What it does to the return
A bank charge or a filing feeYesMakes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required
An accounting or legal costYesReported as an expense, with the loss carried forward
Interest credited on a balanceNoInvestment income, so the year is not nil
Revenue of any kindNoEnds the nil year whatever the costs were
A dividend paid or receivedNoNot nil, and handled by gondaliyacpa.ca

The nil GIFI balance sheet checker shows what Schedule 100 has to carry on a quiet year, and the dormant corporation test settles the nil question across every entry at once.

The Loss Is Only Real Once the Year Is Filed

A year of costs with no revenue produces a loss, and that loss is only established by the filed return for that year. Leaving the year unfiled leaves the loss unestablished, which is the quiet cost of skipping a year that felt too small to bother with.

Schedule 8 and the loss continuity schedule travel with the return and are inside the fee. The loss continuity on a nil return checker covers what happens to a loss while its year sits unfiled.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a year with expenses but no income still nil?

Yes, for this service. Costs going out do not make a year active. What ends a nil year is something coming in: revenue, interest credited on a balance, rent or a dividend either way.

Do the expenses make extra schedules necessary?

They make GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required, because something sat on the books during the year. Those schedules are inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year rather than charged separately.

What happens to the loss from a year like that?

It is established by the filed return for that year and carried on the loss continuity schedule. A year left unfiled leaves its loss unestablished, which is one reason to file a small year rather than skip it.

title: Never Traded Corporation Checker | The First Return
content:
First Return

Never Traded Corporation Checker

A corporation that never started still owes a first return. This dates it from the incorporation date and the 53-week limit.

Computed datesCarries the 53-week limitSchedule 24 includedThree inputs

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

Your corporation

Enter the incorporation date and answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Clock Starts at Incorporation

A corporation that was set up and never used is still a corporation. Its first tax year begins on the incorporation date, not on the day it first trades, and the return for that year is due six months after whichever year-end it adopts.

Nothing arrives to prompt anyone, which is why the first contact is often a demand to file covering several years at once.

What a First Return Carries

On the returnNeeded on a never-traded year?Why
Schedule 24, first-time filer informationYesIt is a first return, whatever happened in the year
GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141Where shares were issued or costs were paidShare capital, cash or an incorporation cost puts a balance on the books
Schedule 50, shareholder informationWhere a shareholder holds 10 per cent or moreA single shareholder holds 100 per cent, so Schedule 50 applies
The T2 ShortWhere every condition holdsIncluded in the fee rather than charged separately

The 53-week first tax year checker tests a proposed year-end against the limit, and the first T2 year-end options generator lists every month-end the first year may use.

A Parked Corporation Is No Different

A corporation incorporated to hold a name, a structure or a single asset is on the same footing as one that trades. Every year since incorporation is a tax year, and each one is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Where several of those years are outstanding, they are filed oldest first, because a T2 carries figures forward from the year before it. The catch-up filing schedule generator lays them out in order.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a corporation that never traded have to file?

Yes. The first tax year begins on the incorporation date whether or not anything happened in it, and a T2 is due six months after the year-end. With no activity the return is nil, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

How late can the first year-end be?

The first tax year cannot exceed 53 weeks from the incorporation date, so the checker dates the latest year-end the limit allows and the return due on it.

Does a never-traded first return still need schedules?

Schedule 24 is on every first return. The GIFI schedules are required where shares were issued or any cost was paid, and Schedule 50 applies to any shareholder at 10 per cent or more, which a sole shareholder always is.

title: Restarting a Dormant Corporation | Which Years Stay Nil
content:
Dormant to Active

Restarting a Dormant Corporation Checker

Trading again does not change the quiet years behind it. Which years are still nil returns, and which one is not.

Three answersSeparates the quiet yearsSays when it is a referralCovers the unfiled years

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

Where the corporation is now

Answer the questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Quiet Years Do Not Move

A corporation that goes back to trading carries its history with it. The years it spent dormant are still tax years, each with its own return, and each of those returns is still a nil return however busy the corporation becomes afterwards.

So a restart splits the record rather than resetting it: quiet years behind, active years ahead, and a line between them that falls on a year-end rather than on the day the first invoice went out.

Which Year Goes Where

YearNil?Filed byFee
Each quiet year before the restartYesThis service$300.00 plus HST per tax year
The year activity resumed, if nothing came in yetYesThis service$300.00 plus HST per tax year
The year revenue, rent or a dividend arrivedNoGondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca$350.00 plus HST per year
Every year after that, while tradingNoGondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca$350.00 plus HST per year

The dormant corporation obligation checker covers what a dormant year still owes, and the unfiled years checker lists which of the quiet years are still open.

Clear the Quiet Years First

Where quiet years are still outstanding, they are filed oldest first, because a T2 carries figures forward from the year before it. Filing the active year on top of a gap leaves the gap exactly where it was.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does restarting a dormant corporation change the old years?

No. Each dormant year is still its own tax year with its own return, and each is still a nil return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year. Trading again changes the years ahead, not the years behind.

Who files the year the corporation restarted?

If revenue, rent or a dividend arrived in that year, it is not a nil year and it is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year. If nothing came in yet, it is still a nil return here.

Should the quiet years be filed before the active one?

Yes, oldest first. A T2 carries figures forward from the year before it, so the years are assessed in the order they fell due and a gap left behind stays open.

title: Loss Continuity on a Nil Return | What Carries Forward
content:
Schedules

Loss Continuity on a Nil Return Checker

A nil year claims nothing against a loss and still reports it. What an unfiled loss year does to the balance.

Three answersCovers an unfiled loss yearSchedule 8 inside the feeSays what a nil year reports

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

Your loss position

Answer the questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Loss Is Established by a Filed Return

A loss is not a fact about a year. It is a figure reported on the return for that year, which means a year left unfiled leaves its loss unestablished however clearly the books show it.

That is the quiet cost of skipping a small year. The expense was real, the loss was real, and without the return there is nothing on the record to carry forward to a year that could use it.

What a Nil Year Does With a Loss

PositionOn the nil returnInside the fee?
An earlier loss, its year filedReported on the loss continuity schedule and carried forwardYes
An earlier loss, its year unfiledNothing to carry: file that year first, oldest firstYes, each year at its own fee
A loss arising this year, from costs with no revenueEstablished by this return and carried forwardYes
No loss at allThe schedule reports a nil balanceYes
Income this year to claim a loss againstNot a nil year, so not one we fileNo

The Schedule 8 CCA requirement checker covers the depreciable property side of the same schedule set, and the required schedules checker lists the whole set a nil return carries.

A Nil Year Claims Nothing

A nil year has no income, so there is nothing for a loss to be applied against and nothing is claimed. The balance is reported and carried, which is the only thing a nil year can usefully do with it.

Schedule 8 and the loss continuity schedule are inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year. What falls outside is a year with income in it, which is not a nil return and is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a nil return still carry the loss continuity schedule?

Yes. The schedule reports the balance carried forward even where the year claims nothing against it, and a nil balance is reported as a nil balance. It is inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

What happens to a loss while its year is unfiled?

It is not established. A year is only established by its own filed return, so the loss has nothing on the record to carry forward from. Filing that year, oldest first, is what puts it there.

Can a nil year use an earlier loss?

There is nothing to use it against. A nil year has no income, so the balance is reported and carried rather than claimed.

Each Corporation Is Its Own Taxpayer

Holding several quiet corporations does not consolidate them. Each is its own taxpayer with its own Business Number, its own fiscal year-end and its own return for every tax year it has existed, and the fee is $300.00 plus HST per tax year on each of those returns.

So the arithmetic is corporations multiplied by years, which is the figure people are usually surprised by when they own three or four dormant companies rather than one.

What the Multiplication Looks Like

There is no reduced rate for several corporations or several years in one sitting: every return is prepared, reviewed and transmitted on its own. The unfiled years cost calculator prices one corporation across its years, and the dissolve or keep filing cost calculator sets years of filing against winding one up.

The Deadlines Multiply as Well

Where the corporations share a fiscal year-end, every return falls due on the same date, six months after it. Where they do not, each has its own deadline and there are as many dates to hold as there are corporations.

The corporate deadline calendar generator dates one corporation’s year end to end, and running it once per corporation is the practical way to hold several at once.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there a discount for filing several corporations?

No. $300.00 plus HST per tax year is charged per tax year per corporation, because each return is prepared, reviewed by a CPA and transmitted separately. Five corporations with one quiet year each is five returns.

Can several corporations be filed on one form?

Each corporation is filed as its own return against its own Business Number. The calculator totals them so the figure is known before any of them starts.

Do they all share a deadline?

Only where they share a fiscal year-end. Otherwise each return is due six months after that corporation’s own year-end.

title: Post-Dissolution Return Checker | What Is Still Owed
content:
Wind-Up

Post-Dissolution Return Checker

A dissolved corporation stops having tax years. Which periods are still owed up to the dissolution date, and which never arise.

Computed deadlineSays what never arisesCovers the earlier yearsThree inputs

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

The wind-up

Enter the dissolution date and answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Tax Years Stop at the Dissolution Date

Dissolution ends the corporation, and with it the sequence of tax years. The final period runs to the dissolution date and its return is due six months after that date. No period after it is a tax year, so there is nothing further to file.

What dissolution does not do is clear what came before. A year that was unfiled on the day of dissolution is unfiled afterwards, and it is still the corporation’s year.

Which Periods Are Owed and Which Are Not

PeriodReturn owed?Deadline
Each full tax year before the final oneYes, until filedSix months after each year-end
The final period, ending on the dissolution dateYes, the final T2Six months after the dissolution date
Any period after the dissolution dateNoNo tax year arises
A year already filed and assessedNoClosed, unless adjusted

The final T2 return due date calculator dates the final return on its own, and the dissolution timeline calculator puts it in the order of the wind-up steps around it.

The Earlier Years Come First

A T2 carries figures forward from the year before it, so outstanding years are filed oldest first and the final return goes last. Filing the final return on top of a gap leaves the gap where it was, and an unfiled year blocks both a clearance certificate and the dissolution itself.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a dissolved corporation owe returns for later years?

No. The final period ends on the dissolution date and no tax year arises after it, so there is nothing further to file.

When is the final T2 due?

Six months after the date of dissolution. Where that date falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday recognised by the Canada Revenue Agency, a return received by the next business day is on time.

Does dissolution clear the years that were never filed?

No. Those years stay open and stay the corporation’s, and they block a clearance certificate and the dissolution itself until they are filed.

title: Acquired Corporation Unfiled Years | What Came With It
content:
Change of Owner

Acquired Corporation Unfiled Years Checker

A tax account belongs to the corporation, not its owner. Which years came with the purchase and which are yours.

Two dates inSplits the years at the purchaseSays what it does not decideCovers the catch-up order

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

The corporation you bought

Enter both dates and answer the question.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Account Belongs to the Corporation

A corporate tax account is the corporation’s, not the shareholder’s. Buying the shares changes who owns the corporation and changes nothing about the account: the Business Number, the fiscal year-end and every outstanding year stay exactly where they were.

So a quiet corporation bought cheaply can arrive with several unfiled years attached, and those years are outstanding on the same account the new owner’s returns will go to.

Which Years Came With It

PeriodWhose yearsStill owed?
From incorporation to the purchaseThe corporation’s, under the previous ownerYes, until each one is filed
From the purchase onwardThe corporation’s, under youYes, as each falls due
A year already filed and assessedThe corporation’sNo, closed unless adjusted
A year before incorporationNobody’sNo tax year exists

The tax years since incorporation calculator counts the years from the incorporation date, and the unfiled years checker lists which of them are open.

What This Checker Does Not Decide

Buying a corporation has consequences beyond the filing calendar, and this tool does not reach them. It answers one question: the outstanding years belong to the corporation and are still outstanding after it changes hands.

Where a quiet year is outstanding, it is a nil return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, filed oldest first. Where a year had activity under either owner, it is not a nil year and is handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do unfiled years come with a corporation you buy?

Yes. The tax account belongs to the corporation rather than to its owner, so every outstanding year is still outstanding after the shares change hands, on the same account the new returns go to.

Who is responsible for the previous owner’s unfiled years?

The returns are the corporation’s to file, and the corporation is now yours. Each quiet year is a nil return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, filed oldest first because a T2 carries figures forward.

Does the fiscal year-end change when a corporation is sold?

The year-end on the Canada Revenue Agency record is the one the return has to match, and buying the shares does not change it. A return filed to a different date is rejected for the year-end.

title: Sole Shareholder Corporation Checker | Schedule 50
content:
Shareholders

Sole Shareholder Corporation Checker

A single shareholder holds 100 per cent, which is above the Schedule 50 threshold. What a one-person corporation reports.

Three answersSchedule 50 always appliesNames the GIFI triggerInside the fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 3, 2026

Your corporation

Answer the three questions above.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

One Hundred Per Cent Is Above Ten

Schedule 50 lists every shareholder holding 10 per cent or more. A sole shareholder holds the whole corporation, so the test is met by a wide margin and the schedule is always on the return.

It reads like a rule for corporations with outside investors, and the one-person company is the case where it most reliably applies.

What a One-Person Nil Return Carries

On the returnRequired?What triggers it
Schedule 50, shareholder informationAlways, for a sole holderA single shareholder holds 100 per cent
GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141Where anything sits on the booksShare capital, cash, a shareholder loan or a cost paid
Schedule 24, first-time filer informationOn a first returnThe corporation’s first tax year
The T2 ShortWhere every condition holdsInside the fee rather than charged separately
Schedule 8 and loss continuityWhere there is a balanceDepreciable property or a loss carried forward

The Schedule 50 shareholder threshold checker measures several holdings against the threshold, and the shareholder register completeness checker checks what the register has to hold for each one.

The Shareholder Loan Is a Reporting Question Here

A balance owed either way makes the GIFI schedules required, and it does not stop the year being nil. That is the reporting answer, and it is the one these pages give.

What a loan balance means for tax turns on periods and a rate this service does not carry, so it is not answered here rather than answered badly. The due to versus due from shareholder checker shows which side of the balance sheet the balance sits on.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does a one-person corporation file Schedule 50?

Yes. The schedule lists every shareholder at 10 per cent or more, and a sole shareholder holds 100 per cent, so the holding is always listed.

Do shares issued at incorporation make the GIFI schedules necessary?

Yes. Share capital sits on the balance sheet, which makes GIFI Schedules 100, 125 and 141 required even on a year with no activity. They are inside $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Does a shareholder loan stop the year being nil?

No. A balance in either direction makes the GIFI schedules required and leaves the year nil. What the loan means for tax is a separate question this service does not answer.

Two Numbers, Issued by Two Bodies

A corporation carries two identifiers and they are not interchangeable. The Business Number identifies it to the Canada Revenue Agency and carries the program accounts hanging off it. The corporation number identifies it to the register it was incorporated under.

Confusing the two is a filing problem rather than a paperwork one: a return transmitted against the wrong identifier cannot be assessed against the right corporation.

What We Confirm Before the Return Is Prepared

You do not need either number to hand to start. The filing form takes the corporation name, and the Business Number and incorporation date are confirmed against the corporation record before the return is prepared.

What matters more than either number is the name: the return carries the exact legal name the register holds, corporation number and suffix included, and a mismatch is one of the common causes of a refused transmission. One corrected transmission is included in $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the Business Number the same as the corporation number?

No. The Business Number is issued by the Canada Revenue Agency and carries the program accounts; the corporation number is issued by the register the corporation was incorporated under. The T2 uses the Business Number and the registry annual return uses the corporation number.

Do I need my Business Number to start?

No. The filing form takes the corporation name, and the Business Number and incorporation date are confirmed against the corporation record before the return is prepared.

What happens if the legal name does not match the register?

It is one of the common causes of a refused transmission, whichever number is on the return. The return carries the exact legal name the register holds, and one corrected transmission is included in $300.00 plus HST per tax year.
